title: Human capital: theory / task evidence / marketplace test
text:
“Human Capital, AI, and Labor Commoditization”
With Niuniu Zhang (UCLA Anderson)
Has AI changed the value of human capital in freelance labor markets?
– Theory: Standardizing tasks reduces reliance on worker know-how, making
workers more substitutable (Fukui, Nakamura, and Steinsson, 2026).
– AI narrows performance gaps: larger gains for lower-performing writers and
novice support agents (Noy and Zhang, 2023; Brynjolfsson et al., 2025).
– Our test: In Upwork, a freelance marketplace, does hiring shift away from
workers with stronger human capital and toward lower-priced workers?
5

title: Burnout evidence, one bullet at a time
text:
Burnout reduces the firm’s productive capacity
Exhaustion, detachment and reduced efficacy under chronic stress (WHO, 2019).
– Lower performance: meta-analysis of 45 studies links burnout to worse job
performance (Corbeanu et al., 2023).
– Lost productive time: burnout predicts longer sickness absence in a
longitudinal study of 201 managers (Schaufeli et al., 2009).
– Model-based cost estimate: about $5 million annually for a U.S. firm with 1,000
employees (Martinez et al., 2025).
Productivity gains can be offset by lost productive capacity.
14

title: Employee protection, one bullet at a time
text:
Investing in employee protection
– HubSpot offers coaching, therapy and meditation as part of its effort to prevent
burnout (HubSpot, 2021).
– Greater control over work schedules and more supervisor support can reduce
burnout: a randomized initiative with 867 IT workers (Moen et al., 2016).
– Among 1,012 employees, autonomy and support were associated with a weaker
link between job demands and exhaustion or cynicism (Bakker et al., 2005).
Can better conditions protect employees when incentives also respond?

title: Employee welfare: Proposition 1 / illustration
text:
1. Employee welfare can fall, then rise
Better technology makes each unit of work more valuable.
Does competition allow employees to enjoy those gains?
Proposition 1
Without burnout (ρ = 0), welfare W ∗ is strictly increasing in θ for
weak γ and strictly decreasing for strong γ.
With burnout, W ∗ strictly decreases on an initial θ interval and
strictly increases on a higher interval, where x∗ falls and mean
burnout time rises.
Sufficient conditions. Fixed γ. For the reversal: sufficiently strong γ, high ρ, and
small employee burnout cost ϕw > 0.

title: Closing implications, three points revealed in order
text:
Implications
– Consider looser ranking quotas or more weight on collaboration.
PayPal dropped individual ratings to reduce stress (PayPal, 2022).
– Keep performance incentives fixed as work conditions improve.
Work redesign: more control and clearer goals (Kelly and Moen, 2020).
– With modest technology gains, less competition may be more welfare-efficient
than more wellness spending.
Individual wellness programs can overlook broader work conditions (Croft
et al., 2024).
